newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING TIE RED WINGS IN LAST 25 SECONDS OF REGULATION.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING TIE RED WINGS IN LAST 25 SECONDS OF REGULATION.

text.p: Detroit Red Wings goaltender Mike Vernon made a mistake that cost his team a win, but coach Scotty Bowman was not pointing fingers.
Vernon's mistake allowed Daymond Langkow to score the tying goal with 25 seconds left in regulation, lifting the Tampa Bay Lightning into a 3-3 deadlock with the Red Wings.

With Detroit protecting a 3-2 lead in the final minute, Alexander Selivanov dumped the puck into the left corner of the Red Wings zone. Vernon tried to move the puck around the boards, but Tampa Bay's Shawn Burr chopped it to the side of the net where Langkow easily put it into the vacated cage.
"I was just coming in and was surprised that the puck was on my stick," Langkow said. "Burr did all the work."

"It was the right play to come out and play it," Vernon said. "I interfered with Burr and then it just went through me. I should've played the puck. I'll take full responsibility for that goal, it was definitely my fault, I screwed up."
"You've got to make a decision and live with it," Detroit coach Scotty Bowman said. "I don't finger a player, it's a team game."
The Lightning led 2-1 entering the third period but Sergei Fedorov scored at 8:39 to tie it. Tomas Sandstrom tallied with 5:33 remaining to give the Red Wings a 3-2 edge.
David Shaw and Rob Zamuner scored first-period goals for Tampa Bay, which has just two wins in its last 11 games (2-8-1).

"There are two schools of thought, we were leading but then they took it away," Tampa Bay coach Terry Crisp said. "But we were able to come back and get a point. It's like a double kick to the stomach, one's a good one and one's a bad one."

David Shaw gave Tampa Bay a 1-0 lead in the first period but red-hot Brendan Shanahan scored his 38th goal, a power-play tally, at 9:06 to tie it. Shanahan has nine goals during a five-game goal-scoring streak.
Vernon finished with 26 saves while Rick Tabaracci stopped 32 shots.

In New York, Wayne Gretzky failed to end his scoring drought but he set up two goals as the Rangers rallied for a 2-2 tie with the New Jersey Devils, who extended their unbeaten streak to a franchise-record 11 games (6-0-5).
Martin Brodeur made 30 saves for the Devils to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 12 games (8-0-4), while Mike Richter had 38 saves for the Rangers.
Steve Thomas and Valeri Zelepukin scored for the Devils.
Gretzky's career-long goal-scoring drought reached 20 games, but he took his league-leading assist total to 61.

Gretzky made a brilliant pass to set up Niklas Sundstrom in the second period to tie the game 1-1. Brian Noonan tied it 2-2 at 4:29 of the third off a deflection of a Gretzky pass just 1:44 after the Devils took the lead on Zelepukin's goal.

In Anaheim, rookie defenceman Dan Trebil scored his first NHL goal and later added an assist in a three-goal first period and Guy Hebert made 30 saves as the Mighty Ducks beat the Edmonton Oilers 5-1.
Joe Sacco and Paul Kariya also scored in the first period and Teemu Selanne and Steve Rucchin added second-period goals for the Ducks, who have won all three meetings with the Oilers this season.
Dean McAmmond tallied the lone goal for the Oilers, who played without top scorers Doug Weight (injured ankle) and Andrei Kovalenko (back spasms).
At Los Angeles, Mike Modano scored the go-ahead goal with 2:03 left and Andy Moog made 34 saves, leading the Dallas Stars to a 2-1 victory over the Kings, who are winless in their last six games.
Dallas, the Central Division leader, improved to 4-1 in its last five games and crept within six points of Colorado for the best record in both the Western Conference and the NHL.
The Stars are 3-0 against the Kings this season.
The Kings remained in a last-place tie with San Jose in the Pacific Division. Their winless streak rose to 0-4-2.

On Long Island, Mark Recchi and Valeri Bure scored in the final two minutes of the first period and Jose Theodore made 36 saves to make it stand up as the Montreal Canadiens rolled to a 4-1 victory over the New York Islanders.
Brian Savage and Sebastien Bordeleau added insurance goals in the third period for the Canadiens, who won for just the fourth time in their last 14 games (4-7-3).
Derek King scored for the Islanders, who missed a chance to tie a season-high with three straight wins.
In St Louis, Pierre Turgeon's second-period goal on the power play snapped a tie as the Blues surrendered a two-goal lead before defeating the Chicago Blackhawks 4-2.
Eric Daze and Ulf Dahlen scored for the Blackhawks, who lost for just the second time in eight games.
